answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to finish a chain of dependent modular squarings: no step can begin before the previous result is known. GPUs may process separate clones in parallel, but cannot shortcut an individual chain, so each clone still incurs sequential elapsed time and hardware cost. A Wesolowski proof makes the delay efficient to verify; hollow identities gain no shortcut, and a trellis of clone chains still consumes parallel capacity, one sable link at a time.
